perspectives.label: Analytical Observer
perspectives.comment: The theorem, once proven, is a fundamental mathematical truth.

perspectives.label: Naive Map Maker
perspectives.comment: Even someone unfamiliar with advanced mathematics will find that they cannot construct a planar map requiring more than four colors.

commentary.narrative_context: The Four Color Theorem states that no more than four colors are required to color the regions of any map on a plane such that no two adjacent regions have the same color. This is a fundamental topological constraint.
key_agents: Analytical Observer: Sees the theorem as a mathematical truth.
Naive Map Maker: Discovers the constraint empirically.
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness and suppression are both zero because the theorem is a fundamental constraint, not an imposed one. The theater ratio is zero because there is no performative aspect. Accessibility collapse is 1.0 because the constraint is universally accessible. Resistance is 0.0 because there is no resistance to a mathematical truth.
commentary.perspectival_gap: There is no perspectival gap. All observers classify the theorem as a mountain. Even those not mathematically sophisticated will be unable to construct a planar map requiring more than four colors.
commentary.directionality_logic: Not applicable since this is a mountain classification. There are no beneficiaries or victims.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: Not applicable, since this is a mountain.
